comment: The glow of the world view (D-188, D-910, D-915). The world draws in HDR 2D, and a pixel glows when its brightest channel passes the threshold, in basis points of linear light, where 10000 is full white. The load keeps the brightest lit art of every light setup below the threshold, so a sprite or a tile never glows (F-47). Each fire that glows draws a small rectangle over its flame above the threshold, and the rectangle pulses on a wave of pulse_ticks, which takes away pulse_depth of its light at the low (D-913). The knee is the span above the threshold where the glow grows to full. The intensity, the strength, and the seven levels, from the sharpest blur to the widest, go to the glow of Godot. The owner halved the intensity of round 1 (D-915). The glow is a smooth bloom, outside the palette (D-911). The fog draws above the glow, so it never glows (D-916).
